subject: Redwood migration & compatibility: next tests vs hyperscalers
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@techfin.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood migration & compatibility: next tests vs hyperscalers

Thanks again for the call today, Daniel — great to meet you and Aisha. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can validate migration risk and perf/cost delta vs your current hyperscaler endpoints.

Recap from our discovery:
- Current infra: TechFin runs core inference on Hyperscaler A managed endpoints (OpenAI-esque API proxy).
- Main asks: 1) functional parity for our prompts (OpenAI-compatible API), 2) throughput/latency at 99th percentile, 3) cost per 1M tokens, 4) support for streaming and function/tool-calling, and 5) secure deployment (VPC).
- Primary workloads: customer support summarization + document search + transaction routing; typical prompt lengths ~150-400 tokens, peak concurrency ~120 qps.

Proposed next tests (attached test plan + prompt diffs):
1) API compatibility smoke: swap SDK -> call Redwood OpenAI-compatible endpoints with your existing client for 50 representative prompts (we included a prompt-diff file). Goal: zero semantic regressions and no SDK-level changes beyond base URL/key swap.
2) Latency and throughput A/B: run the same workload against Hyperscaler A endpoints and Redwood Dedicated (we can provision a short reserved capacity trial). Measure p50/p90/p99 and tail latency under burst.
3) Cost estimate run: run sample traffic replay (30m) to produce cost projection (tokens, infra).
4) Feature parity: streaming, function calling, and embeddings correctness (similar dimensions).

Attachments: redwood-vs-hyperscalers-brief.pdf, compatibility-test-plan.xlsx, prompt-diff-samples.json

Next steps I suggest:
- You sign off on the test plan by EOD Wed 6/30.
- We provision a 2-week Dedicated trial and a shared test harness (we'll share a short script to replay requests).
- Rishi to provide a quick matrix on expected quantization/model variants that map to your latency/cost targets.

If that sounds good I'll loop Rishi and Neha to schedule a short runbook call tomorrow to sort credentials and VPC access items.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Exec | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0182

From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@techfin.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Aisha Gupta <aisha.gupta@techfin.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood migration & compatibility: next tests vs hyperscalers

Thanks Marissa — this looks great and aligns with what we discussed. A few clarifications from our side: 
- For the API compatibility smoke, we want to confirm we don't need to change our prompt engineering (no tokenization surprises) and that function calling behaves the same with our current function schemas.
- For embeddings, we want cosine similarity stability vs our existing embeddings across typical docs.
- On security: we'll need SOC2 evidence and a basic network diagram for the VPC flow as part of the procurement packet.

We'll sign off on the plan pending a short call tomorrow. We can run the 50 prompt smoke internally — will need the endpoint + test harness script.

Daniel
Director, Platform Engineering
TechFin Systems
daniel.park@techfin.com | +1 (617) 555-0147

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@techfin.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 08:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood migration & compatibility: next tests vs hyperscalers

Daniel — perfect. Looping in Rishi and Neha for the technical/runbook items. Rishi: can you confirm availability to support the smoke run and provide the mapping of model flavors (e.g., 8-bit quantized vs fp16) that we'll recommend for parity vs Hyperscaler A? Neha: can you pull the SOC2 evidence summary and a VPC network diagram we can share?

Quick practical notes for the smoke run:
- Endpoint + creds: we'll provision a short-lived API key and a staging URL (OpenAI-compatible surface) — no SDK changes expected beyond base_url and api_key. We'll also provide a small python script that uses the OpenAI SDK to send the 50 prompt samples (prompt-diff-samples.json).
- Tokenization: we've included a tokenization report for the first 10 prompts in the prompt-diff file; early look shows 1-2 token deltas on longer system prompts due to tokenizers, but no semantic drift in our QA checks. We'll surface any that need minor prompt tweaks.
- Function calling: Redwood supports the same JSON schema for function definitions; we'll test both synchronous and streaming function call flows.

I'll kick off provisioning as soon as Daniel confirms the test window.

Thanks,
Marissa

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Daniel Park <daniel.park@techfin.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood migration & compatibility: next tests vs hyperscalers

Thanks Marissa — quick notes from infra/modeling side before the run: 
- Model mapping: recommend starting with 'redwood-1-small' (fp16) as the closest functional match to your Hyperscaler A baseline for latency, and 'redwood-1-medium-q8' (8-bit quantized) for a cost-optimized run. We'll surface inference perf numbers in the test report.
- Streaming & function calls: we've validated streaming parity for our streaming protocol and function-calling JSON schema; we'll include end-to-end examples in the runbook.
- Tokenization diffs: as Marissa noted, expect tiny token count differences on system prompts; we will include a token-normalization helper you can run pre-flight to flag any outliers.
- Security pack: Neha will attach SOC2 summary and VPC diagram to the HubSpot deal; for the trial we'll use a private dedicated node in us-west with IP allowlist and short-lived keys.

I'll be available for the runbook call tomorrow at 10:00am PT. If that doesn't work, propose 2:00pm PT.

-Rishi
SVP, Solutions Engineering | Redwood Inference
